request.prompt:
PRIMARY REQUIREMENT: draw the exact S13 knight recoiling while retaining his right-hand sword in EVERY hurt pose. The fifth row is the only intended repair. This is a NEW independent drawing from the two exact upstream images, never a previous sprite sheet. Other rows supply the established import layout.

Use case: identity-preserve / game animation frame art.
Asset type: ONE complete directional sprite sheet for a flat 2D isometric game. Actual transparent PNG, 1536 by 2048 canvas. Six columns and eight rows; 48 isolated full-body frames in equal 256 by 256 cells. No text, labels, numbers, grid lines, scenery, shadows or watermark. Each frame centered at its cell foot pivot, full weapon sweep inside cell; wide transparent gutters, no overlap between cells.
Input image 1: the CURRENT #1 chosen gameplay screen G15. Match its dark dirty granular drawn texture, soot contours and muted slate/taupe/wine palette. Input image 2: its EXACT S13 original Guarin character, identity and costume authority. Draw this exact character, no redesign: gigantic worn flat-topped enclosed riveted greathelm with one tiny black eye slit and a few breathing holes; tiny squat body, short wrapped brown limbs, ragged wine scarf/cape, dull mail, belt, small straight one-handed sword in RIGHT hand, worn wood/iron kite shield on LEFT arm with faded narrow red stripe. Head/helmet nearly half standing height. No visible face or eyes, no plate body armor. Same gear sizes/material marks across every frame.
Only FLAT HAND-DRAWN 2D frame art. No 3D render, sculpture, shiny miniature, smooth plastic shading, realistic adult proportions or comic panels. The source's gritty mottled texture must remain, not clean vector coloring. Dim neutral overcast values, readable on light/dark backgrounds, no baked night lamp or heroic rim light. Fixed elevated orthographic camera about 45 degrees above ground; clear helmet top and foreshortened tiny torso. Pose direction is below; camera never moves. Keep all 48 figures at the SAME tiny-body proportion and scale.
DIRECTION: S — Facing directly toward the viewer, down-screen. Front visor visible, symmetric frontal top view. Sword in anatomical RIGHT hand at screen-left; left-arm shield at screen-right.
Chronological frames left-to-right. Exactly eight rows, top-to-bottom:
1 IDLE: six distinct restrained breathing/weight-settle drawings; same feet, barely moving cape; seamless loop.
2 WALK: six distinct gait keyframes; right contact, right down/passing, left contact, left down/passing, recovery; both boots and knees visibly change, gear follows weight; in-place seamless loop, never translate whole character across cell.
3 SWORD CUT: ready, wind-up, strong anticipation, blade contact arc, follow-through, return to ready. Sword remains straight, distinct arc; left shield on arm throughout.
4 GUARD: lower shield begins raising; shield reaches guard; stable guarded pose; slight guarded breath; begin lowering; lowered ready. Keep sword safely withdrawn. Frames 3-4 will loop as hold.
5 HURT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE: six chronological recoils with the SAME SWORD visibly clenched in the anatomical RIGHT glove throughout, on screen-left. (1) shoulders jolt, tiny knees begin bending, blade held low down-left. (2) peak recoil: head/body lean back and the right sword arm extends down-left, glove CLOSED around the hilt; show the entire straight blade clear of the torso, pointing toward lower-left ground. (3) off-balance deepest flinch, knees bent; right hand still clenches the same hilt, blade remains fully visible down-left, NEVER an empty open palm. (4) returning upright, right arm brings the sword back low. (5) small weight-settle, sword at low ready. (6) neutral ready with the same right sword and left-arm shield. Both boots stay on the ground; do not fall or die. Left shield remains attached on screen-right throughout and may tilt with the recoil; it never switches hands. SAME frontal facing toward screen-bottom and same huge closed helmet, tiny body and weapon dimensions in all six. Hurt moves the body and weapon together; it does not delete, hide, detach, shorten or drop the sword. No blood, broken equipment or extra props.
6 DEATH: knees buckle; falling; hits ground; rolls/settles; motion nearly stops; entirely still prone corpse. Helmet stays on, gear intact, no second helmet or lost limbs. Full body must actually lie down.
7 INTERACT: reaches toward an object at chest/ground reach; makes contact; small manipulation; withdraws; settles; ready. Do not add an object or remove gear.
8 PRAYER: lowers body toward kneel; kneels; quiet bowed held prayer; slight bowed breath; rising; upright ready. Frames 3-4 will loop as channel. Closed helmet remains huge, boots/body tiny.
The sheet is 48 NEW DRAWN animation poses of the exact reference knight. References are upstream style/design only, never paste the previous image. No camera/orientation/proportion changes between columns. Preserve anatomical handedness for this direction.

inspection: Parent viewed actual output: six fifth-row hurt poses retain the straight sword in the right glove, visible down-left during peak recoil; left shield stays attached on screen-right. Closed oversized helmet and tiny body retained. Only HURT is selected; other rows remain excluded to preserve existing motion. Camera and foot alignment remain provisional.
